title: Usage records missing, impossible or unpriced
description: A self-reported session (a file exported afterwards, such as a self-exported chat log, a chat app's export or an ATIF trajectory, not a log a known harness wrote while it ran) must carry the provider's usage on at least the published min_self_reported_usage_share (half by default) of its assistant messages, so a self-reported session with no usage fails; a session handed over by an agent whose tool keeps no session record (a self-export carrying "handed_over") is held to no share of usage, and the usage it carries is held to the rules below as any. A file in Claude Code's or Muse Code's session format that has an assistant message and no usage record, or in Claude Code's without the version Claude Code writes on every line, is judged as a self-reported session: both harnesses record the provider's usage with every response. Its token counts must be the provider's own, not rounded, estimated or repeated figures: of 8 or more counts of 100 or more (each response's input and output), 4 in 5 that are multiples of 10, or half that are multiples of 100, fail; and of 6 or more usage records, one pair of counts (the input with its cache reads and writes, and the output) on every record, or, neighbouring repeats taken as one response, 6 or more responses with no more different pairs than half their number, fail. Its output must be no more than a model produces in the time its own timestamps span: with 3 or more usage records, the output of all but its largest response (each response's output tokens, or its visible bytes over 16 where those say more) is at most the published max_self_reported_tokens_per_sec (500 by default) for each second from its first timestamp to its last, plus 5. The Muse app's own session files record no usage, so the Muse app sessions of an entry must carry at least the published min_muse_app_usage_rows (one by default) usage rows across them: the rows Muse keeps in its database, which the agent attaches with bundle --muse-usage. Those rows are held to the round-figure, repeated-count and output rules above, never to the share of assistant messages: Muse records one row per delivered message, not one per response. Then at least the published min_priced_share (every record by default) of the upload's usage records must price: the pricing rows bill the model each record names, and a record they do not price passes at $0 where its session ran the model on the entrant's own machine (a local runtime such as Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp, or a loopback server, that the session records, never a model's name or the provider a self-exported chat log names). That $0 counts for this check alone, never toward the entry's build cost; any other record the rows do not price is unpriced. An upload of logs a known harness wrote with no usage record (Cursor, which records none) has nothing to price and passes; its build cost is unknown, never $0.
